name: Standard atomic weights (IUPAC/CIAAW) for mass/mole conversion

source.located: CIAAW/IUPAC 'Standard Atomic Weights 2024' (www.ciaaw.org/atomic-weights.htm), 'Abridged Standard Atomic Weights 2024' (abridged-atomic-weights.htm), 'Isotopic Compositions of the Elements 2024' (isotopic-abundances.htm); the tables are based on the 'Atomic Weights 2021' report (Prohaska et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 94, 573 (2022), not itself opened) with the 2024 Gd/Lu/Zr revisions. Supporting source for the solar-material test: Asplund, Grevesse, Sauval & Scott 2009, arXiv:0909.0948, sec. 3.10, 3.12, Table 1, Table 3.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on the three CIAAW web pages (full tables returned verbatim) and on arXiv:0909.0948 (pp. 20-24, 42, 44, 46). WebFetch of ciaaw.org is egress-blocked. Afterwards the alphaXiv quota ran out, so the CIAAW per-element history pages (argon.htm, zirconium.htm) were never opened.

published_statement: CIAAW: 'Standard atomic weights are CIAAW recommended values for atomic weights applicable to all normal materials.' Elements with well-documented natural variation get an interval, e.g. Ar°(Ar) = [39.792, 39.963]; the rest get value(U), e.g. Zr 91.222(3) (revised 2024), Fe 55.845(2), P 30.973761998(5). Abridged values are 'quoted to five significant figures unless such precision cannot be attained', e.g. H 1.0080, O 15.999, Ar 39.95+-0.16, Tl 204.38, Pb 207.2+-1.1.
published_hypotheses: NORMAL MATERIAL: the values apply to 'normal materials', i.e. terrestrial sources (CIAAW footnote g: 'Geological and biological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material'; footnote m: commercially fractionated material may deviate substantially).

INTERVAL: for 14 elements (H, Li, B, C, N, O, Mg, Si, S, Cl, Ar, Br, Tl, Pb) the standard is an interval, not a single value; the abridged table gives a single conventional value with a +- that is not a standard uncertainty.
UNCERTAINTY: the value(U) entries mean normal-material values lie within +-U 'with great certitude' (Possolo et al. 2018, cited by CIAAW, not opened).

REVISION: the table is revised over time. The CIAAW page states that the standard isotopic compositions of Yb (2015), Ta (2017), Ir (2017), Ar (2017), Hf (2019), Pb (2021), and Gd, Lu, Zr (2024) have been revised since the 2013 report.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED 'normal material' at stockgate.py:441-447 (solar), 499-510 (solar_hybrid), 519-527 (jupiter_hybrid), 759-771 (condensed_budget) and stock.py:240-246 (cosmic). The terrestrial standard weights convert Asplund-2009 SOLAR number abundances to mass fractions. A09 (arXiv:0909.0948 sec. 3.10) adopts terrestrial IUPAC isotopic ratios for most elements, but it uses non-terrestrial ratios for H, He, N, Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe. Solar-system weights computed from A09 Table 3 and AME2020 differ from the tree's: Ar 36.275 vs 39.948 (-9.19%), Ne 20.131 vs 20.180 (-0.24%), H -1.5e-4, He -1.4e-4, N -1.2e-4. The effect is COMPUTED as immaterial: 0 binder flips in 30 payload x destination cells, max factor shift 1.78e-4, regimes and the stock.py destination rank unchanged. The solar Ar mass fraction is 9.2% too high as tabulated (7.34e-5 vs 6.67e-5).

Taking every interval element at its lower bound gives 0 flips (max shift 1.48e-4); at its upper bound, 0 flips (max shift 8.09e-3, mostly from Li at 6.997 vs 6.94).

The thinnest margins are Cl (Abar 35.484, margin 0.016; 35.478-35.490 over the whole CIAAW Cl interval) and Zn (65.450, margin 0.050). rederivation.outcome: PASS, 0 failures (output in rederive/standard-atomic-weights.out). A: all 63 tree entries are consistent with CIAAW 2024. Two are superseded in form: Ar 39.948 (the 2024 standard is an interval containing it) and Zr 91.224 (vs 91.222(3), within U). B: independent re-derivation of the 18 stock.py weights as sum x_i m_i, with CIAAW 2024 representative isotopic compositions (READ) and AME2020 masses (the tree's READ capture). All agree within the interval width or 3U; the worst relative difference, 4.0e-3 for Li, comes from taking the midpoint of Li's wide composition interval. Si and Ca agree to 2e-5. C: solar-system isotopes (A09 Table 3) move no binder, regime or rank. D: massform H-A holds for all 14 HUMAN elements; smallest margin Cl 0.016. E: interval ends move no binder.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The standard atomic weights are measurements revised as data arrive, and the table READ here documents that directly: the argon standard became an interval in 2017, once radiogenic Ar-40 variation in normal materials was documented, and zirconium was revised in 2024. So the earlier single values were incomplete in exactly M's sense. The evidence runs against this mattering here: both revisions keep the tree's values inside the new standard (Ar 39.948 in [39.792, 39.963]; Zr 91.224 within 91.222 +- 0.003), and no stockgate or stock.py verdict moves (0/30 flips, max shift 2.5e-5). The larger data gap is one the tree created, not the authors: the CIAAW values are explicitly for normal (terrestrial) material, and the tree applies them to solar material. Given the solar isotopic data (A09 Table 3), Ar moves by 9.2% and Ne by 0.24%, and still no verdict moves (max shift 1.8e-4). The data that came later changes digits, not conclusions.
grade_evidence: The published result holds on 'normal materials', and every one of the tree's 63 values is consistent with CIAAW 2024 (re-derived from isotopic compositions and AME2020 masses; script PASS). The tree drops the normal-material hypothesis by applying the table to solar and Jovian abundances (stockgate.py:441-527, stock.py:240-246). It also flattens 14 interval standards to unnamed point values. That is the NARROWED clause ('a hypothesis the tree drops'). It is NOT WRONG, and it moves nothing: with solar-system isotopes, CIAAW-2024 abridged values, or all interval ends, there are 0 binder flips in 30 payload x destination cells, the regimes and destination rank are unchanged, and the max factor shift is 8.1e-3 (interval upper ends), 1.8e-4 (solar) and 2.5e-5 (2024). Ar 39.948 and Zr 91.224 are stale in form only; each lies within the current standard. Nothing is repaired in the tree.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners name the normal-material hypothesis and the conventional-value convention (or use solar-system weights for the solar columns), with a READ citation to CIAAW. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a future CIAAW revision that moves an element outside the tree's value AND changes a binder. The computed margins make that implausible for a mass/mole conversion: the nearest effect is 9.2% on Ar, which binds nothing. To WRONG: only a computed binder or regime flip, and none exists on any tested table. massform H-A would fail only if Cl's mean nucleon number reached 35.5; it is 35.478-35.490 over the whole CIAAW interval.
